title.note: Compiled 2026-09-24. confidence: documented = stated in source; approximate = read off plot, derived, or proxy site; estimate = not found, reasoned value.

name.value: Las Campanas Observatory (Magellan site = Cerro Manqui)
name.note: Magellan telescopes sit on Co. Manqui; GMT is on Co. Las Campanas.

latitude_deg.note: Wikipedia 29d00m54s S. IRAF obs-db 'lco' entry (du Pont area) gives -29.00333; Angeloni+2023 LCO sky-camera site 29d00m41.98s S.

longitude_deg.note: Wikipedia 70d41m30s W. IRAF obs-db 'lco' gives 289.29833 E (= -70.70167).

elevation_m.note: Wikipedia LCO 2380 m; lco.cl/CfA pages say ~2400 m for Magellan; IRAF 'lco' entry 2282 m is the du Pont level. Use 2380-2400 m.

V_LCO_measured.note: Sky-quality-camera zenith (ZA<5 deg) value at LCO on 2019-11-24, Angeloni+2023 Table 5 (Table 4 gives 22.02). ~11% of radiance is artificial light (ALAN).

UBVRI_adopted_CTIO_proxy.note: CTIO 1992-2006 means (Krisciunas+2007 Table 6); CTIO is ~100 km S of LCO with similar altitude/climate. Consistent with LCO V=21.95. sigma ~0.2 mag night-to-night.

UBVRI_Walker_CTIO_newmoon.note: Walker 1987 table (NOAO Newsletter Mar 1994). Page currently offline; values as indexed by search engine and also used as 'sky mag' column in LCO IMACS 2022 handout.

ugrizy_AB_CerroPachon_proxy.note: Rubin/LSST SMTN-002 dark-sky model for Cerro Pachon; proxy for LCO.

LCO_ETC_sky_model_newmoon.note: ESO SkyCalc v1.4.3 output used by the official LCO ETC (day 0: Sun-Moon sep 0 deg, solar flux 130 sfu). NIR broadband values from SkyCalc are unreliable for LCO; prefer FourStar values.

IMACS_handout_sky_mags.note: Sky magnitudes tabulated next to IMACS imaging zero points (2022 handout). I=19.9 in manual.

NIR_broadband_LCO_FourStar.note: 'Typical background' on Magellan/Baade FourStar page. AB-Vega offsets from same page: J1 +0.68, J +0.92, H +1.36, Ks +1.85.

NIR_H_duPont.note: Chen+2002 'typical H-band sky brightness of 14.7 magnitudes' at du Pont/LCO.

NIR_interline_continuum_LCO.note: Sullivan & Simcoe 2012 (FIRE, R=6000) dark-sky means; +0.15/-0.18 mag systematic. H 'continuum' mostly OH wings; zero-OH extrapolation H_AB~19.4. Moon raises Y,J continuum.

u.note: Swope+SITe3, CSP-I 2004-2009, Krisciunas+2017 Table 4; +-0.057 (std of distribution).

U.note: Not measured at LCO; ~0.9x u-band (Johnson U bluer cut-on is similar); typical Chilean value.

R.note: Interpolated between r (0.103) and i (0.059) at lambda_eff ~6400-6500 A.

I.note: Slightly below i (0.059) at lambda_eff ~8000 A. BiSON LCO Ic median 0.033 (arXiv:1707.06647) suggests clear-sky minimum.

Ks.note: Not in CSP table; typical dry-site Ks 0.05-0.08.

stability_note.value: Nightly extinction terms very stable over 5 CSP campaigns
stability_note.note: Justifies fixed coefficients in a simulator; add ~0.02 mag rms nightly jitter.

percentiles_Co_Manqui.note: GMT site-testing DIMM 2005-2008, Magellan site; Co. Las Campanas 0.42/0.50/0.63/0.79/0.99.

lognormal_sigma_ln.note: Derived from GMT quartiles: sigma_ln = ln(0.79/0.51)/1.349 ~ 0.32-0.34; Floyd mean/std gives ~0.30.

ground_layer_Manqui_percentiles.note: ~65% of seeing from ground layer in median conditions.

seasonal.value: Summer/fall better; driven by free atmosphere

outer_scale_L0.note: Average L0 inferred at Magellan; vK model with L0=25 m bounds the data.

median_science_images.note: IMACS/LDSS3/MagIC frames (DIPSF); mean 0.585 +- 0.150. Guide cameras median 0.688.

fit_vs_DIMM.note: Magellan sharper than DIMM 69% of time (98% when DIMM>=1").

photometric_fraction.note: +-0.04; ~50% in austral winter, higher in summer.

useful_time_fraction_longterm.note: Average photometric 60-65%, ~85% of potential time useful (telescope logs).

wind_limit_close.note: 'current operating limit for the Magellan telescopes is 15.6 m/s'. ~1% of useful time at Manqui above it.

wind_direction.note: Bimodal; SW stronger in summer and early night.

humidity_close_limit.note: Magellan limit NOT published. Proxy: ESO La Silla rule (RH>90% or T within 2 C of dew point, wind>20 m/s). Many sites use 80-85%; simulate 85-90%.

dewpoint_margin_close.note: Proxy from ESO La Silla rule; not published for Magellan.

reopen_rule.note: Proxy: ESO 3.6m requires 30 min (2.2m: 45 min) below limits, esp. for humidity. Magellan rule not published.

PWV_percentiles_all.note: Winter median 1.4 mm; summer 5.1 mm. Stable within a night.

effective_collecting_area.note: ATEL=306383.8 cm^2 in every Magellan PARAM file of the official LCO ETC. Cross-check: pi/4*6.5^2*(1-0.29^2)=30.39 m^2.

value.auxiliary: three f/11 aux ports on centre section

blind_pointing_rms.note: 'Baade telescope sets to an rms accuracy of a few arcseconds' (Dressler, Sutin & Bigelow).

elevation_lower_limit.note: NOT FOUND in public docs (not on cited LCO page). Typical for 6.5-m alt-az; practical science limit usually airmass<=2 (el>=30 deg). Also avoid zenith keyhole (~>87 deg) for alt-az rotator speed.

slew_rate_azimuth.note: NOT FOUND (not on cited LCO page). Typical of 6.5-8 m alt-az mounts.

slew_rate_elevation.note: NOT FOUND (not on cited LCO page). Typical of 6.5-8 m alt-az mounts.

slew_settle_time.note: NOT FOUND; typical settling plus dome catch-up. Dome rotation may dominate for large az moves.

setup_guide_and_active_optics.note: Guider + Shack-Hartmann setup 'will take a few minutes, limited by the time for the Shack-Hartman sensor to converge'. Simulate 3-5 min after slew.

operations_window.value: TOs on duty sunset to dawn; twilight calibrations by TO/observer
operations_window.note: Science typically between ~12 deg twilights for faint optical work; flats in civil/nautical twilight.

science_twilight_convention.note: Not a written LCO rule; common practice (NIR and bright targets start at -10 to -12 deg, faint optical at -15 to -18 deg).

instruments.note: Instrument complement changes; check LCO schedule.

dark_current.note: Value assumed in LCO ETC PARAM files (=3.6 e-/hr); no measured value found in IMACS docs.

full_well.note: NOT FOUND. Estimate = 65535 ADU x gain (assumes 16-bit ADC); physical well of E2V 2Kx4K ~150-200 ke- would not be reached.

longslit_widths.note: 'long-slit slitmasks with widths ranging from 0.7" to 2.0" are kept on hand' - exact list not found; intermediate widths assumed. Centerfield slit-viewing slits 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0/1.3".

mask_swap_cassette_reload.note: Pre-arranged change of the loaded mask complement.

multislit_mask_alignment.note: Early design 10-15 min (Dressler SPIE); 5-10 min per set-up (Dressler+2006 SPIE abstract); 'typically 10 minutes or less' incl. slew (Dressler+2011). Iterative: field image ~10 s, mask image, offsets until negligible.

longslit_acquisition.note: Not documented; field image + slit image + imacs_slit_align offset + disperser insertion.

alignment_image_exposure.note: Longer in poor seeing; 1x1 (f/2) or 2x2 (f/4) binning.

total_throughput.note: Read off handout Fig.1 (GD71, 0.6" slit). PASP: 30-35% in H,K; ~25% incl. slit losses; <20% in z,Y.

recommended_exposure.note: No hard max documented. OH lines suffice for lambda-cal only if >8-10 min (F1). Practice: 900 s SUTR (PypeIt, Masters+2014), 15-20 min between nods (Simcoe+2011).

nod.note: A position 1-1.5" left of slit center.

slit_length.note: 12"-wide slit is 56" long; MIT specs say 50", handout 1'.

zero_point.unit: AB mag giving 1 DN/s per extracted pixel (J,H)
zero_point.note: Handout Fig.2 range AB 19-20.8; Burgasser+2011: ~3-4 mag fainter than echelle.

recommended_max_exposure.note: Avoid K saturation / OH non-linearity. Quasar surveys use low gain SUTR 600-900 s (practice).

saturation.note: => ~26 ke- (high) and ~120 ke- (low, full well). Low gain nonlinear >28000 ADU.

read_noise.note: Current LCO manual vs PASP (on-sky +10-20%). Sources disagree; use ~15 e- for Fowler-1 as compromise.

read_noise_vs_SUTR_length.note: Read off MIT plot; PypeIt default ~5 e- for ~900 s SUTR (echelle).

readout_overhead.note: Fowler effective exposure = requested + 10.6 s; SUTR exposure must be multiple of 10.6 s (min 21.1 s).

dark_current.note: +-0.0004 (~2.5 e-/hr). Y/J read-noise limited, H/K sky limited.

acquisition_overhead.note: NOT FOUND. Components: 30 s slit-viewer frames, blind offsets 0.2-0.3" rms, 'trust but verify' ~0.15".

telluric_practice.value: A0V star near airmass/position of target between science targets, 5-20 s Fowler-1, AB nod; ThAr arc at every pointing (flexure ~1 px)

telescope.value: Clay (Magellan II), East Nasmyth, gravity-invariant (no rotation)
telescope.note: Tilted 30 deg: slit along atmospheric dispersion at ZA=30 deg.

detectors.value: 2 x e2v CCD44-82 2048x4096, 15 um, 2 amps each; red is deep-depletion

wavelength_coverage.note: Handout: red to 9500. Dichroic ~4950 A. Blue orders 71-106, red 37-70.

read_noise.note: GUI section: fast ~4.7 e-, slow ~3.7 e-. e2v lab 2.5 e-. ETC: 2.36 (blue), 2.64 (red) slow.

readout_time.note: Same manual's GUI section says fast full frame 95 s, slow 160 s. Telescope may move during readout; arcs can be taken during slews.

full_well.note: Linear to ADC saturation: ~59 ke- at 0.9 e-/DN (estimate, 16-bit).

rotator_modes.note: Mode meanings inferred from names and instrument examples (LDSS3 27.5 EQU for N-S slit; -62.5 HRZ parallactic).

scriptable_TCS_interface.value: No public documentation of a scriptable/remote TCS command API
scriptable_TCS_interface.note: Only instrument-side helpers that send offsets to the TCS are documented (FIRE IDL fatv_* commands; IMACS/LDSS3 alignment tools produce offsets the TO applies). FIRE: 'Macros are not currently supported'.

setup_forms.value: Instrument setup form >= 14 days before run; masks >= 6 weeks

reference.note: doi:10.1086/132921; equations transcribed from ADS scan; cross-checked with DESI specsim implementation https://github.com/desihub/specsim/blob/main/specsim/atmosphere.py

eq3_scattering_airmass.note: Use for both sky position and Moon in eq15 (per KS91 recommendation).

eq14_extinction_airmass.note: For directly observed objects (not scattered light).

eq9_moon_magnitude.unit: V mag; alpha = phase angle deg (0 = full)
eq9_moon_magnitude.note: For |alpha|<7 deg multiply B_moon by 1.00-1.35 (opposition effect; 'about 35% brighter' at exact full). Apogee/perigee changes m by up to +-0.12.

accuracy.note: 8-11% vs Russian daytime data; Patat 2003 finds KS91 reasonable for B,V,R,I at Paranal.

table2_test_values_nL.note: Moon ZA 60 deg, k=0.172, rho measured along great circle through Moon and zenith (rho=60 is zenith). Use as unit test.

method_Noll2012.value: B_moon,R/M(lam) = fR/M(rho) I*(lam) t(lam)^Xmoon (1 - tR/M(lam)^X0); I*(lam) = solar spectrum scaled to KS91 V; fR = 10^5.70(1.06+cos^2 rho); fM = 10^(7.15 - rho/40)
method_Noll2012.note: Rayleigh/Mie separated with their own transmission curves; factors 2.2 and 10 vs KS91 tuned to Paranal. alpha ~ arccos(1 - 2 FLI). Systematic <~10%, statistical 10-20%.

moonlight_colors_SkyCalc_fullmoon.unit: mag (m_band - m_V of moonlight excess, Vega)
moonlight_colors_SkyCalc_fullmoon.note: Derived here: SkyCalc full moon (moon sep 45 deg, alt 45 deg) minus new-moon sky, per band, from LCO ETC readme files. Recipe: m_moon,band = m_moon,V(KS91) + color.

moonlight_colors_Walker_fullmoon.note: Derived from Walker 1987 table (day 14 minus day 0). U excess looks implausibly strong; prefer SkyCalc colors.

Walker_table.unit: mag/arcsec^2 vs days from new moon (CTIO)

SkyCalc_fullmoon_LCOETC.note: Day-14 sky used by LCO ETC (Sun-Moon sep 180, moon-target 45 deg, moon alt 45 deg, zenith target).

formula.value: m(zeta) = a0 + a1 (zeta-95) + a2 (zeta-95)^2, zeta = 90 - h_sun (deg), valid 95<=zeta<=105
formula.unit: mag/arcsec^2 at zenith (|alpha|<=40 deg), Moon down
formula.note: Paranal FORS1; includes night-sky contribution; night level reached at zeta~105-106.

coefficients.note: gamma = linear slope (mag/arcsec^2/deg) over 95-100; x ~0.23 deg/min at Paranal equinox -> 0.22 (I) to 0.28 (U) mag/arcsec^2/min.

values_at_minus18_extrapolated.note: Outside fit range (zeta=108); U/B extrapolate fainter than dark sky -> clamp to dark sky. Recommended: F_sky = F_dark + max(0, F_fit(zeta) - F_dark_Paranal) for zeta<=105, else F_dark.

colors_note.note: Twilight bluer than night sky; sodium/[OI] flash lines; OH dominates red after astronomical twilight begins.

within_night.value: No systematic decline after twilight on average (0.03-0.04 mag/hr in B/I at most); ~0.1 mag sinusoidal fluctuations on ~0.5 hr time scales; occasional 0.7 mag excursions

zodiacal_correction.unit: mag (avg ZL contribution in Paranal dark means)
zodiacal_correction.note: Sky darker at high ecliptic latitude.

solar_cycle.value: Dark sky brightens with 10.7 cm solar flux (airglow)

OH_free_fraction_vs_R.note: Read off Simcoe+2008 SPIE Fig.1 (+-3%). MOSFIRE PDR: only ~10% of H free at R~1300; 'R~3000 required for effective OH suppression'.

true_continuum_fraction.note: Sullivan & Simcoe 2012 (R=6000); Ellis & Bland-Hawthorn 2008 (R=10^4, incl. grating scatter). 75% of J,H within 10x continuum.

wavelength_scaling.value: FWHM proportional to (lambda/500nm)^-0.2; r0 proportional to lambda^1.2

ESO_ETC_IQ.value: FWHM_IQ = sqrt(FWHM_atm^2 + FWHM_tel^2 + FWHM_ins^2); FWHM_atm = s X^0.6 (lam/500)^-0.2 sqrt[1 + F_Kolb 2.183 (r0/L0)^0.356]; r0 = 0.100 s^-1 (lam/500)^1.2 X^-0.6 [m]; F_Kolb = 1/(1+300 D/L0) - 1; FWHM_tel = 0.000212 lam[nm]/D[m] arcsec
ESO_ETC_IQ.note: s = DIMM seeing at 500 nm, zenith. Set FWHM_atm=0 if sqrt argument <0. ESO: L0=46 m, F_Kolb=-0.981644 (VLT).

Tokovinin2002_vK.note: Valid for L0/r0>20 to +-1% (quoted in Martinez+2010 Eq.4 and Floyd+2010 Eq.1; original PASP 114, 1156 not fetched - bot check). FWHM_K = 0.976 lambda/r0. Independent of D for L0/D<=500.

L0_values.note: Paranal 1-sigma 13-37 m (Martinez+2010); ESO 46 m from van den Ancker+2016.

example_LCO.note: ESO-ETC formula with L0=25 m, D=6.5 m; consistent with Floyd predictions.

delivered_IQ_model.value: FWHM_delivered^2 = FWHM_atm^2 + FWHM_optics^2 (+ dome/wind terms); Magellan optics 0.17" (Nasmyth LDSS3) / 0.30" (IMACS)

Racine1996_efolding.note: <f(dt)> = <f(inf)> [1 - exp(-dt/tau)]^gamma with f=|w(t+dt)-w(t)|/(w(t+dt)+w(t)); f(inf)=0.218, tau=17+-1 min, gamma=0.66; Mauna Kea free atmosphere (SCIDAR). log-normal sigma_log10=0.175 (sigma_ln 0.40).

Herriot2010_TMT_PSD.note: TMT used 100-tap AR generator; 'good seeing lasting hours followed by jumps on minutes'.

Kornilov2018.note: Forecast scatter 1.8x smaller than unconditional at 1 h, 1.4x at 2 h.

persistence_forecast_RMSE.note: De Sepibus, Masciadri+2026; last-10-min mean as forecast.

within_night_std_SPM.note: San Pedro Martir DIMM; no trend with time of night.

LCO_specific_time_scale.note: NOT FOUND for LCO; Skidmore+2009 not retrievable (bot check).

value.optional: add power-law f^-1.43 component for jumps

recommended_simulator_model.note: Synthesis: total sigma_ln 0.33 matches LCO quartiles (0.34); 1-h change ~0.16" consistent with VLT persistence RMSE 0.17" and SPM within-night sigma 0.19".
